title: Query Rewriting: Intent Into Retrieval
objective: After this lesson you will be able to expand vague shopper queries (multi-query, step-back), extract filters (budget, category, SKU), and prove rewriting gains with before/after retrieval comparisons.
why: 'Something comfy for long walks, cheap' retrieves nothing literally — yet a human clerk hears cushioning + walking + budget instantly. Rewriting translates shopper language into retrievable form: expansions for vocabulary, step-back for abstractions, extracted filters for constraints. Retrieval quality is bounded above by query quality; rewriting raises the ceiling.

blocks.text: Vague in, concrete out: three rewrites

**Multi-query**: one vague query → several concrete sub-queries ('cushioned walking shoes', 'budget walking shoes under $100', 'walking shoe return policy'), retrieve per sub-query, fuse (Ch.4). **Step-back**: abstract the principle first ('what defines walking comfort? cushioning + support'), retrieve the principle, then instantiate. **Filter extraction**: pull structured constraints (budget < $100, category shoes, size 9) for metadata filtering alongside text retrieval.

blocks.caption: Deterministic expansion + filter extraction; models handle the tail

blocks.text: Rewriting must earn its latency: run gold vague queries with and without rewriting, compare hit-rates. Wins concentrate on vocabulary-mismatch and multi-constraint queries; precise SKU queries gain nothing (and pay expansion cost). Gate rewriting on vagueness signals (no exact tokens, hedges like 'something', multiple intents) — precise queries skip straight to retrieval.

blocks.title: Log rewrites with the query
blocks.text: Persist each query alongside its rewrites and the vagueness signals that triggered them. Rewrite logs turn 'why did it search that?' from archaeology into lookup — and the signal distribution (which vagueness dominates) tells you what to fix next: vocabulary (expansions), structure (filters), or corpus (nothing to retrieve).

blocks.title: Rewrite the vague
blocks.note: Run it: the vague query gains the maxPrice filter (rewrite-worthy true via filters); the SKU query stays single with empty filters (skip rewriting, retrieve directly). Expansions live in the full lesson version — filters alone already gate correctly. Gate by vagueness signals, not habit.

items: Multi-query expansion, step-back principles, filter extraction — three rewrites for three vagueness kinds
Gate rewriting on vagueness signals; precise queries skip to retrieval
Prove with before/after hit-rates on vague gold queries — rewriting earns its latency or ships without it

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice rewriter on both queries and map outputs. (b) Add a size-9 constraint to the vague query and confirm the size filter extracts. (c) Write the skip rule: which query shapes bypass rewriting entirely, and what breaks if they don't?
hints: Vague: expansions + maxPrice 100, rewrite-worthy true. Precise: single query, no filters, rewrite-worthy false.
Size extraction: /size\s*(\d+)/i on '...size 9...' → filters.size 9. Confirm alongside maxPrice.
Skip: SKU/exact-name/single-fact queries — rewriting them adds latency and synonym noise to already-perfect retrieval.
exercise.why: Gating (rewrite-worthy signals) plus filter composition plus skip rules make rewriting a measured subsystem — applied where vague, absent where precise.
exercise.code: // Rewrite-gate pattern: vagueness signals → expand; exact tokens → skip.

quiz.q: 'Something comfy, cheap' retrieves nothing. First move?
options: Rewrite: expand vocabulary (cushioned/budget), extract maxPrice filter — translate intent before retrieval
quiz.explain: Vague queries fail literally. Expansion + filters convert shopper language into retrievable form.

quiz.q: SKU query through the rewriter gains synonyms. Verdict?
options: Harmful noise on solved retrieval: gate rewriting to vague queries; precise ones skip
quiz.explain: Rewriting taxes precise queries with latency + synonym drift for zero gain. Vagueness-gated application only.

quiz.q: Step-back ('what defines walking comfort?') helps when?
options: Abstraction gaps: query asks instances, corpus discusses principles — retrieve the principle, then instantiate
quiz.explain: Instance-principle mismatch defeats literal retrieval. Step-back bridges abstraction levels before instantiating.

summary: Expand vocabulary, extract filters, step back abstractions — gated by vagueness, proven by before/after. Retrieval quality starts at query quality.
next: Candidates retrieved — now order them ruthlessly: reranking with fusion, budgets, and top-k discipline. Next: precision at the top.
